Peranganad, Peranginad, Parunganaad, Paranginaud, Parunganaud, Paungnaad, Purganaud, Perunganaud, Paranganad, Perangada, Porunganaad, Perunga Nad, Peringa Naad, Poranad, Poringar, the NE division of the Nilgiris in pre-British times, centred on Kotagiri and roughly coterminous with the modern Kotagiri taluk, ca 35,742 ha., 233.1 km? is plateau land, and 103.6 km? is slopes; locale of a distinct dialect of the Badaga language (q.v.; the division now contains Kengare, Ko:damu:le, Jakkata/Jakkato:, Jakkana:ri/ Jakka:re, Ta:ndana:du, Torehaṭṭi, De:na:du, Niruguve/Neduguve, Pedduva, Bandime, Ba:mudi, Bebbe:ṇu, Mi:de:ṇu, Sakkata/Sakkatore/Sakkato:, Suḷḷligu:du and Hubbatale communes; name in existence before to 1809; the etymology is problematic, whether < Ta. perangi+tBad. na:du+si:me, ‘Frank, foreigner+division+lang’, or < per+ rangatna:du+si:me, ‘great+Ranga+divisiontlanď, or perange + na:du+si:me, ‘pepper berry+division+lanď’, or < Kota poranj +Bad. ka:du+si:me, ‘outertforest+land’; the first perhaps referring to an unproven 17th Cent. incursion of Catholic missionaries from Satya-
